note: Clean pass, one caveat. The instrument was administered in Polish; item_text/option_text hold the Polish wording verbatim from S3 Appendix (10.1371/journal.pone.0229354.s004, 'Questionnaire (native version: Polish language)') and the _translated columns hold that appendix's own English version. The IRW item codes are the S2 Dataset (.s006 XLSX) header strings verbatim, which are a THIRD, slightly different English rendering of the same six stems (code 14 reads "I feel that it's possible that one day..." where the appendix reads 'I feel that it is possible that one day...', and code 16 reads 'I am happy that my profile can also be so good.' where the appendix reads "I'm happy that my profile can also be so good."). Item codes must be read as join keys, not as the administered wording. Likewise the S2 Dataset stores anchors as 'Strongly disagree/Disagree/Rather disagree/Neither agree or disagree/Rather agree/Agree/Strongly agree', a terser English rendering than the appendix's 'I totally disagree'..'I totally agree'; the shipped option_text_translated follows the appendix, and resp 1..7 is the ascending-agreement coding that data/jablonska_2020_instagram.py's LIKERT_MAP applies to those label strings. The questionnaire prints no instruction text for these items - only the part heading 'Part I. Instagram usage.' covering items 1-25 - so instructions and section_prompt are left blank rather than filled with a heading.

The paper's Fig 2 per-odor accuracies come from the S1 'Monell Data' sheet (n=1163) and do NOT match this IRW table, which is built from the separate S1 'NIH Tolbox Sensory items' sheet (n=845): play doh 72.0% vs 48.4%, lemon 81.3% vs 92.3%, smoke 81.3% vs 71.5%, flower 94.1% vs 86.3%; the other five agree to ~2 points. The two sheets carry different ID systems (MONELL codes vs BHR login) so the rows cannot be linked, and the difference is too large and too item-specific to be a subsampling effect. The IRW table is internally consistent (its Yes counts sum to the 'NIH Toolbox ODOR ID scores' sheet's OdorIDScore for all 845 rows), so this is a property of the deposit, not of the extraction - but a reader comparing Fig 2 to the table will find they disagree. Live IRW per-item accuracy (item_stats.R, n=845 every item): lemon 92.3, play doh 48.4, bubble gum 87.9, chocolate 69.2, popcorn 83.3, coffee 92.8, smoke 71.5, natural gas 94.0, flower 86.3. Recomputed from the S1 'Monell Data' sheet (n=1163): lemon 81.3, play doh 72.0, bubble gum 85.6, chocolate 70.2, popcorn 85.9, coffee 91.5, smoke 81.3, natural gas 95.9, flower 94.1. Differences: play doh +23.6, lemon -11.0, smoke +9.8, flower +7.8; the other five within 2.6 points. A deposit-level disagreement between two sheets of the same S1 file, not an extraction error, and not a text-vs-table mismatch -- correctly kept off the public issues page.

Item text and anchors come from the S1 File .sav's own variable and value labels (PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0152479, CC BY 4.0); the IRW item codes ARE that file's column names, so the mapping is authoritative at the source. Two disclosed deviations from a literal copy of those labels: an invisible U+200E left-to-right mark was stripped from OPRO_3, and runs of whitespace were collapsed. The paper's Appendix lists the same 30 items but in a different within-subscale order for Not Harming, Helping/Fairness and Social Justice, so a paper_order alignment would have mis-assigned 12 of 30 items; the labels were used instead. OPRE_5's administered label reads 'A decent person will go out of their way to help another person.' where the Appendix prints 'A decent person will go out of his or her way to help others.' -- the .sav label was shipped as the administered wording. Scale points 2-6 are unlabelled in the source (the .sav stores ' '), so option_text is left blank for them rather than padded. No instrument-level instructions text is published in the paper or the .sav, so instructions is blank. PASS WITH CAVEAT. 6 of 7 items carry verbatim wording from the deposit's own SPSS variable labels (Psychological Well being Mediating Role Updated 24072024.sav, figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.26820745.v4, CC0). AS2's option_text (Strongly disagree..Strongly Agree) is carried over from the identical value labels every other item in the .sav uses; it is an inference, though a narrow one. Instructions were not published anywhere in the deposit or paper and ship as NA. Clean pass, one caveat about table composition. Item text and the 1-5 anchors come from the deposit's own SPSS file (figshare 26820745 v4, 'Psychological Well being Mediating Role Updated 24072024.sav'), whose variable labels name PWB2 and PWB3 and whose value labels give Strongly disagree..Strongly Agree. The .sav's PWB2/PWB3 columns are element-for-element identical (663/663 rows, all 5 level counts equal) to the PWB2/PWB3 columns of the .xlsx that data/jeilani_2024_academic_stress.py actually reads, so the label-to-code tie is confirmed by the data, not just by a shared name. Composition caveat: this table holds only 2 of the study's psychological well-being items, both Ryff autonomy items. The deposit's .xlsx prefixes the remaining Ryff subscale items EM/PG/PL/PRO/SA (Environmental Mastery, Personal Growth, Purpose in Life, Positive Relations with Others, Self-Acceptance), and the IRW processing script read those prefixes as unrelated constructs, so they became the separate live tables jeilani_2024_emotional, _personal_growth, _purpose_in_life, _proactivity and _social_anxiety. Verified by element-wise column identity: the .sav's PWB4/PWB5/PWB6 are exactly the .xlsx's EM3/PG1/SA1. Rights check: the Ryff scales are distributed free of charge on request from Carol Ryff (UW-Madison Institute on Aging); no enforced fee and no quotable no-redistribution clause was found, and IRW's wording came from a CC0 deposit's own SPSS labels, so no rights block applies. Administration language is not stated anywhere in the deposit; only English wording exists in it, so language and the _translated columns are left out. [ORCHESTRATOR, Step 5b] Re-checked the public_note's claim independently against the cached .sav and .xlsx: CONFIRMED element-wise over all 663 rows. sav PWB1 is identical to xlsx SSF1 (label: 'I get the emotional help and support I need from my family' -- an MSPSS family item, not Ryff); sav PWB4 = xlsx EM3 ('I am good at managing the responsibilities of daily life' = Ryff Environmental Mastery); sav PWB5 = xlsx PG1 ('life has been a continuous process of learning, changing, and growing' = Personal Growth); sav PWB6 = xlsx SA1 ('I like most parts of my personality' = Self-Acceptance). sav PWB2/PWB3 map to xlsx PWB2/PWB3 and are both Ryff Autonomy items. So the live sibling tables jeilani_2024_emotional / _personal_growth / _purpose_in_life / _proactivity / _social_anxiety are Ryff well-being subscales renamed as unrelated constructs; _social_anxiety and _proactivity are the most misleading. Worth its own issue against the processing script's PREFIX_TO_NAME.
